chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Sa'id ibn Yasar who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): We mix with people from As-Sawad and others, so we sell to them and profit upon them with ten percent, twelve percent, and ten percent to thirteen percent, and we delay that between us and them for a year and similar to it. And the man writes for us upon his house or his land with that wealth which contains the surplus that we took from him as a purchase (security), and he has sold and taken the price from him. So we await him: if he comes with the wealth to a set time between us and him, we will return the purchase (security) to him. But if the time comes and he does not bring us the dirhams, then it is for us. So what do you see regarding that purchase (security)? He said: I see that it is for you if he does not do it, and if he comes with the wealth at the time, then return it to him.

key_terms.أَهْلِ السَّوَادِ: People of As-Sawad (a region in Iraq, often used to denote specific local populations)
key_terms.الشِّرَاء: Purchase/Security (referring to the collateral or item held as security for the debt)
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: Surplus/Profit (the extra amount added to the principal)
key_terms.الْوَقْت: Set time/Deadline (the agreed-upon period for repayment)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on keeping collateral when a buyer defaults on an interest-bearing sale?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the permissibility of *al-shira'* (conditional sale with security) in Shia jurisprudence, addressing a specific commercial practice where buyers secured goods by pledging property while deferring payment. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates this arrangement, ruling that the seller retains the pledged asset only upon the buyer's default, thereby distinguishing it from riba (usury) provided the transfer of ownership is conditional and not automatic. This ruling highlights the pragmatic flexibility of Shia fiqh in accommodating trade customs (*urf*) while ensuring justice in financial transactions.
